policies.name: Block Device Code Flow
policies.description: Blocks OAuth device code flow except for narrowly documented scenarios that cannot use safer authentication methods.
policies.conditions: All users and all resources; Authentication flows: Device code flow; exclude emergency accounts and only documented dependencies
policies.grant_controls: Block access
policies.why_it_matters: Device code phishing sends a victim to Microsoft's legitimate sign-in page while the attacker controls the initiating session. MFA alone does not remove this risk.
gotchas: Review sign-in logs for device code flow and original transfer method before enforcement
Teams devices, Azure CLI, developer tools, and device registration can depend on this flow
If device registration uses device code flow, exclude the Device Registration Service resource rather than creating a broad user exception

policies.name: Block Legacy Authentication
policies.description: Blocks sign-ins using legacy auth protocols (POP, IMAP, older SMTP AUTH, legacy Office clients) that cannot enforce MFA.
policies.conditions: Client apps: Exchange ActiveSync clients, Other clients (legacy auth)
policies.grant_controls: Block access
policies.why_it_matters: Legacy auth is the single most common vector for password-spray attacks because it bypasses MFA entirely. Blocking it closes off a large share of automated credential-based attacks with minimal user impact once modern clients are confirmed in use.
gotchas: Check sign-in logs for existing legacy-auth usage (old scanners, printers, shared mailboxes, cron jobs using SMTP AUTH) before enforcing — this breaks silently and generates helpdesk tickets days later if skipped
Roll out in report-only mode first for at least 1-2 weeks

policies.name: Require MFA for All Users
policies.description: Requires multi-factor authentication for every user on every sign-in, replacing Security Defaults' blanket policy with a tunable one.
policies.conditions: All users (excluding break-glass accounts), all cloud apps
policies.grant_controls: Require multi-factor authentication
policies.why_it_matters: MFA remains the highest-leverage single control against credential compromise. Moving off Security Defaults to a custom policy allows exclusions, reporting, and staged rollout that Security Defaults doesn't support.
gotchas: Always exclude break-glass accounts explicitly
Consider excluding known service accounts and instead securing those via certificate-based auth or managed identities rather than blanket exclusion

policies.name: Require MFA for Admin Roles (Stricter)
policies.description: A tighter MFA requirement scoped specifically to privileged directory roles (Global Admin, Privileged Role Admin, Security Admin, etc.), separate from the general-user MFA policy.
policies.conditions: Directory roles: all privileged built-in roles
policies.grant_controls: Require multi-factor authentication (tighten to authentication strength in Stage 3)
policies.why_it_matters: Admin accounts are the highest-value targets in the tenant. A dedicated policy makes it possible to enforce stronger requirements for this group without over-constraining general users.
gotchas: Keep this policy separate from the general MFA policy, even though they overlap, so it can evolve independently (e.g. adding authentication strength requirements later)

policies.name: Break-Glass Account Governance
policies.description: Not a CA policy itself, but a required companion control: 2+ emergency access accounts excluded from all Conditional Access policies, using long complex passwords (not MFA-dependent), monitored with high-priority alerting on any sign-in.
policies.conditions: N/A — governance control
policies.grant_controls: N/A
policies.why_it_matters: Without a tested break-glass path, a CA misconfiguration (e.g. an overly broad block policy) can lock out every admin simultaneously, including the ability to fix the policy that caused it.
gotchas: Test break-glass sign-in on a fixed schedule (e.g. quarterly) — an untested break-glass account is a false sense of security
Alert immediately (via Sentinel/Defender) on any sign-in to these accounts, since legitimate use should be rare and planned

policies.name: Require Compliant Device for Sensitive Apps
policies.description: Requires an Intune-compliant or hybrid Entra-joined device to access high-sensitivity applications (finance, HR, admin portals).
policies.conditions: Target apps: tier-1 sensitive apps; Users: relevant group(s)
policies.grant_controls: Require device to be marked as compliant OR hybrid Azure AD joined
policies.why_it_matters: Ties access to device posture, not just identity — a stolen credential with MFA satisfied still can't reach sensitive data from an unmanaged device.
gotchas: Requires Intune (or another compliance-capable MDM) already deployed and device compliance policies tuned before this is enforceable without breaking access
Plan a path for BYOD/mobile users (e.g. app protection policies) rather than fully locking them out

policies.name: Session Controls for Unmanaged Devices
policies.description: For sign-ins from unmanaged/non-compliant devices, restricts to browser-based access with no persistent session and limited download/print via app-enforced restrictions (where supported, e.g. SharePoint/OneDrive).
policies.conditions: Device state: not compliant/not hybrid joined
policies.grant_controls: Use app-enforced restrictions; sign-in frequency; persistent browser session = never
policies.why_it_matters: Lets you allow access from personal/unmanaged devices for convenience without leaving persistent, cached credentials or offline copies of sensitive data on them.
gotchas: App-enforced restrictions only work with apps that support them (SharePoint, Exchange Online natively) — verify coverage for your app estate

policies.name: Restrict Guest/External User Access
policies.description: A dedicated policy scoping guest/B2B users to a narrower set of apps and stricter controls than internal employees, rather than inheriting the general employee baseline.
policies.conditions: Users: guest or external users; Apps: explicitly scoped subset
policies.grant_controls: Require MFA; block high-risk sign-ins; may block legacy auth entirely for guests
policies.why_it_matters: Guest accounts are frequently under-governed — they inherit whatever default access exists rather than being deliberately scoped, and are a common blind spot in access reviews.
gotchas: Pair with Entra cross-tenant access settings (inbound/outbound trust settings), not just CA alone, for full control over B2B collaboration

policies.name: Risk-Based Sign-In Policy
policies.description: Uses Identity Protection sign-in risk to require step-up authentication or block access when a sign-in looks anomalous (impossible travel, anonymous IP, unfamiliar sign-in properties).
policies.conditions: Sign-in risk: Medium and above
policies.grant_controls: Require MFA (or block, for High risk, depending on tolerance)
policies.why_it_matters: Moves beyond static rules to real-time behavioral signal — this is what catches a compromised credential being used from a new location even when the device and other conditions look normal.
gotchas: Requires Entra ID P2 licensing
Tune thresholds carefully — Medium risk can be noisy in the first weeks; monitor false-positive rate before tightening further

policies.name: User Risk Remediation Policy
policies.description: When Identity Protection flags a user as high risk (e.g. leaked credentials found in a breach corpus), forces a secure password reset before further access is allowed.
policies.conditions: User risk: High
policies.grant_controls: Require password change (self-service, with MFA required first)
policies.why_it_matters: Automates the highest-priority remediation step (credential reset) without waiting for manual security team intervention.
gotchas: Requires self-service password reset (SSPR) to be enabled and configured tenant-wide, or this policy will lock users out instead of remediating them

policies.name: Phishing-Resistant Authentication Strength for Privileged Access
policies.description: Requires FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business, or certificate-based authentication (not just 'any MFA method') for admin role activation and other high-sensitivity access.
policies.conditions: Directory roles: privileged roles; or PIM role activation
policies.grant_controls: Require authentication strength: Phishing-resistant MFA
policies.why_it_matters: Standard MFA (SMS, push notification) is vulnerable to MFA fatigue attacks and real-time phishing/adversary-in-the-middle proxies. Phishing-resistant methods close that gap for the accounts that matter most.
gotchas: Requires provisioning phishing-resistant credentials (FIDO2 keys or platform authenticators) to admins before enforcement — plan a rollout window
Have a documented break-glass/recovery path for lost hardware keys

policies.name: PIM Role Activation Requires CA Step-Up
policies.description: Ties Privileged Identity Management just-in-time role activation to its own Conditional Access requirement, so activating an admin role triggers a fresh, stronger authentication challenge.
policies.conditions: Authentication context: role activation-linked context
policies.grant_controls: Require authentication strength: Phishing-resistant MFA; may also require compliant device
policies.why_it_matters: Standing admin access is a major risk; PIM reduces the always-on attack surface, but only if activation itself is properly gated — otherwise PIM becomes a rubber stamp.
gotchas: Requires 'Authentication context' configured and referenced from PIM role settings, not just a normal CA app/user condition — this is a two-part setup (PIM + CA), easy to miss the CA half

policies.name: Continuous Access Evaluation
policies.description: Enables near-real-time token revocation for supported apps (Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, Graph) when a user is disabled, password is changed, or risk is detected — instead of waiting for token expiry.
policies.conditions: Tenant-wide setting (not a per-policy condition)
policies.grant_controls: N/A — session/token behavior setting
policies.why_it_matters: Without CAE, a revoked user or a high-risk session can remain valid for up to the token's lifetime (historically up to an hour or more). CAE closes that window to near-real-time.
gotchas: Coverage depends on app/client support — verify which apps in your estate actually honor CAE before assuming full protection

policies.name: Global Secure Access (Network-Layer Conditional Access)
policies.description: Extends Conditional Access-style policy enforcement to network traffic (internet and private app access) via Entra Internet Access and Private Access, not just app sign-in events.
policies.conditions: Traffic profiles: Microsoft 365, internet access, private access
policies.grant_controls: Policy enforced at network layer — compliant device, risk signal, location, etc.
policies.why_it_matters: Traditional CA only governs the moment of sign-in to a cloud app. This extends the same policy engine to general internet-bound and private network traffic, closing the gap CA alone leaves open.
gotchas: Newer capability — licensing and regional availability should be checked against current Microsoft documentation before planning a rollout
Requires client/agent deployment for full coverage, similar to a traditional SASE/ZTNA rollout

policies.name: Conditional Access Policy-as-Code / Change Governance
policies.description: Manages CA policy definitions in source control (via Microsoft Graph API/Terraform provider), with pull-request review, automated report-only testing, and rollback capability, rather than manual portal changes.
policies.conditions: N/A — process/tooling control
policies.grant_controls: N/A
policies.why_it_matters: Manual portal-only changes are hard to audit, easy to make inconsistently, and have no built-in rollback. Treating CA policy like infrastructure-as-code brings the same rigor software changes get.
gotchas: Requires a documented exception process for genuinely urgent manual changes (e.g. active incident response) that bypass normal review — otherwise the process gets circumvented under pressure

policies.name: Enforce MFA Registration Within Grace Period
policies.description: Requires users to register for MFA within a defined grace period after account creation (via Entra's MFA registration campaign / registration policy), rather than leaving registration optional until first prompted.
policies.conditions: All users not yet registered for MFA; typically paired with Identity Protection's registration campaign feature
policies.grant_controls: Require MFA registration before further access is granted, after grace period expires
policies.why_it_matters: An account with MFA required but not yet registered is often still accessible via legacy fallback or is simply blocked in a way that generates help-desk load. Proactively enforcing registration closes the gap between 'policy says MFA required' and 'user actually has a working MFA method.'
gotchas: Set a reasonable grace period (e.g. 14 days) and communicate it — a zero-day enforcement will lock out new hires immediately

policies.name: Block Unsupported Device Platforms
policies.description: Blocks sign-in from device platforms the organization does not officially support or manage (e.g. Linux desktop, or any platform outside an explicit allow-list), reducing the attack surface to known, manageable device types.
policies.conditions: Device platforms: any platform not in the supported list
policies.grant_controls: Block access
policies.why_it_matters: Unsupported platforms usually can't be enrolled in compliance/MDM, so they're an automatic blind spot. Blocking them by default (with an exception process) is simpler than trying to secure something you can't manage.
gotchas: Check for legitimate existing use (developers on Linux, for example) before blocking — build an exception group rather than breaking real workflows

policies.name: Require App Protection Policy (MAM) for Unmanaged Mobile
policies.description: For mobile access from personal/BYOD devices that aren't (and won't be) enrolled in full device management, requires an Intune App Protection Policy — containerizing corporate data within managed apps (Outlook, Teams, etc.) with copy/paste and save-location restrictions — instead of requiring full device compliance.
policies.conditions: Client apps: mobile apps; Device state: not compliant/not hybrid joined
policies.grant_controls: Require app protection policy
policies.why_it_matters: Full device compliance is often unrealistic for BYOD (privacy concerns, unwillingness to enroll personal devices). MAM gives meaningful data protection without requiring the user to hand over device control — usually a better adoption outcome than a hard device-compliance requirement.
gotchas: MAM and full device compliance are different controls — decide which applies per app/user population rather than defaulting to the stricter one everywhere and generating friction

policies.name: Stricter Policy for Azure Management (Portal/CLI/PowerShell)
policies.description: A dedicated Conditional Access policy targeting the 'Microsoft Azure Management' cloud app specifically, with tighter controls (compliant device + MFA, or stronger) than the general app baseline.
policies.conditions: Target resource: Microsoft Azure Management (covers portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, ARM API)
policies.grant_controls: Require compliant device AND multi-factor authentication
policies.why_it_matters: Azure Management access is one of the most commonly under-protected high-value targets — it's easy to protect Microsoft 365 apps and forget that anyone with a valid credential can otherwise reach the Azure control plane directly via CLI/PowerShell/API, bypassing whatever extra scrutiny is applied to the portal UI alone.
gotchas: This single target resource covers all management surfaces (portal, CLI, PowerShell, REST API) — don't assume protecting the portal UI alone is sufficient

policies.name: Terms of Use Acceptance Policy
policies.description: Requires explicit acceptance of a Terms of Use document (acceptable use policy, data handling agreement, etc.) before first access is granted, tracked with a timestamped audit trail.
policies.conditions: New users, or all users on a periodic re-acceptance cycle; often scoped heavily to guest/external users
policies.grant_controls: Require Terms of Use
policies.why_it_matters: Provides a documented, auditable acceptance record for compliance/legal purposes — particularly important for guest and contractor access where a formal acceptance trail may be a contractual or regulatory requirement.
gotchas: Keep the ToU document itself under version control and re-trigger acceptance when it materially changes

policies.name: Conditional Access for Workload Identities
policies.description: Extends Conditional Access to service principals and managed identities (workload identities), not just human users — e.g. restricting a service principal to sign in only from expected IP ranges, or blocking it if Identity Protection flags workload identity risk.
policies.conditions: Workload identities: specific service principals; Location/risk conditions as applicable
policies.grant_controls: Block access outside expected conditions
policies.why_it_matters: Service principals and managed identities are frequently over-privileged and under-monitored compared to human accounts, and are an increasingly common target since they often bypass MFA entirely by design. This closes a gap most tenants leave fully open.
gotchas: Requires Entra ID P2 (Workload Identities Premium) and careful scoping — test thoroughly in report-only mode, since breaking a service principal's access can silently break automation/integrations with no user-facing error to alert anyone

policies.name: Token Protection (Device-Bound Tokens)
policies.description: Binds sign-in tokens to the specific device they were issued to for supported apps (primarily Exchange Online, SharePoint Online), so a stolen token cannot be replayed from a different device.
policies.conditions: Target apps: Exchange Online, SharePoint Online (current supported set)
policies.grant_controls: Require token protection (session control)
policies.why_it_matters: Directly mitigates token theft/replay attacks (e.g. via adversary-in-the-middle phishing proxies or infostealer malware) — even a fully MFA-satisfied token is useless if exfiltrated to an attacker's machine.
gotchas: Supported app/client coverage is still expanding — verify current supported apps and client versions against Microsoft documentation before assuming full coverage

policies.name: Cross-Tenant Access Settings Enforcement
policies.description: Explicitly configures inbound and outbound cross-tenant access settings (which external Entra tenants are trusted for B2B collaboration, and under what MFA/device conditions), governed with the same rigor as internal CA policy rather than left at default trust-everyone settings.
policies.conditions: N/A — tenant-level trust settings, complements rather than replaces CA policy
policies.grant_controls: Trust settings: require MFA/compliant device claims from the external tenant, or restrict to an explicit allow-list of trusted partner tenants
policies.why_it_matters: Default cross-tenant settings are permissive; without explicit governance, B2B collaboration can quietly become a much larger trust boundary than intended.
gotchas: This lives in a separate settings area (Cross-tenant access settings) from standard CA policies — easy to overlook because it isn't in the Conditional Access blade

policies.name: Real-Time Session Control via Defender for Cloud Apps
policies.description: Routes sessions for specified apps through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps' reverse proxy (Conditional Access App Control), enabling real-time monitoring, DLP (block download/copy/print of sensitive content), and session recording for unmanaged-device access.
policies.conditions: Session control: use Conditional Access App Control
policies.grant_controls: Monitor/restrict in real time based on content sensitivity labels and user actions within the session
policies.why_it_matters: Goes beyond allow/block at sign-in to active, real-time control of what a user does within a session — e.g. allowing read-only access to sensitive data from an unmanaged device while blocking download, rather than a blunt all-or-nothing decision.
gotchas: Requires Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps licensing and per-app onboarding to the reverse proxy — not automatic for every SaaS app

policies.name: Insider Risk-Based Access Control
policies.description: Feeds Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management signals into Conditional Access, so a user flagged for insider risk (e.g. data exfiltration indicators, departing employee with elevated risk) automatically faces stricter access controls.
policies.conditions: Insider risk level: elevated/high (via Purview integration)
policies.grant_controls: Require MFA, block download via session control, or block access entirely depending on severity
policies.why_it_matters: Extends adaptive access control beyond external threat signals (Identity Protection) to internal/behavioral risk — closes a gap most CA implementations never address, since CA is usually framed purely around external attackers.
gotchas: Requires Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management configured and populated with policies first — this is an organizational/HR-process-sensitive rollout, not just a technical toggle

policies.name: Restrict Resource Access to Approved Agent Identities
policies.description: Blocks autonomous agent identities unless the agent or its blueprint has been reviewed and approved.
policies.conditions: All agent identities; exclude approved agents or blueprints directly or by custom security attribute
policies.grant_controls: Block access
policies.why_it_matters: Agent identities request tokens without an interactive user. An approval boundary prevents unreviewed agents from receiving organizational access by default.
gotchas: Requires eligible Entra and Agent 365 licensing
Start in report-only mode and validate Microsoft-managed product agents

policies.name: Block High-Risk Agent Identities
policies.description: Blocks token issuance when Entra ID Protection identifies an agent identity as high risk.
policies.conditions: All agent identities; agent risk: high; intended resources
policies.grant_controls: Block access
policies.why_it_matters: Risk detection without enforcement can continue issuing tokens to a compromised agent.
gotchas: Agent risk is a preview capability
Agent identities cannot perform interactive MFA remediation

policies.name: Protect Agent Access on Behalf of Users
policies.description: Applies user-scoped Conditional Access requirements when an agent exchanges a delegated user token for downstream access.
policies.conditions: Users and groups; downstream resources used by agents; application or agent context where supported
policies.grant_controls: Require appropriate authentication strength, device, network, or session controls
policies.why_it_matters: In an on-behalf-of flow the user is the token subject, so agent-identity-only policies do not protect the access path.
gotchas: Do not combine autonomous and on-behalf-of access into one assumed scope
Conditional Access cannot govern direct API-key authentication outside Entra token issuance
